written: 2026-10-26, after exploration (notebook sections 1-6, exploration split only) and before any test touched the confirmation split
multiplicity: Holm-Bonferroni step-down across T1-T4; decisions use the Holm-adjusted p-value
population: established entire homes in the confirmation split: room_type == 'Entire home/apt', number_of_reviews >= 10, valid overall rating
p1_groups: L = host has 10 or more London listings (after duplicate removal); S = host has exactly 1; hosts with 2-9 listings are not used

hype.rule: hyped = at least k hype words, k = the largest count that still covers >= 15% of exploration listings (23.8% have 2+); plain = no hype word; listings with exactly 1 are not used
hype.lexicon: prep.HYPE_WORDS (34 marketing superlatives, fixed before looking at accuracy)

T1.parameter: beta = within-stratum gap in mean overall rating, L minus S
T1.test: OLS with one intercept per stratum and host-clustered (CR1) standard errors; t with G - 1 df
T1.why: two-sided because professional operators could plausibly rate higher (consistent service) or lower (less personal); 0.10 star is a third of the exploration interquartile range (4.62-4.91) and moves a median listing (4.79) across the 4.8 Superhost bar

T2.parameter: theta = common odds ratio, across strata, of a rating below 4.8 for L versus S
T2.test: Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel chi-square (1 df), Mantel-Haenszel pooled odds ratio
T2.why: 4.8 is Airbnb's Superhost rating bar; at the exploration single-host rate of 33.8% below it, an odds ratio of 1.25 means about 39%, i.e. one more listing in twenty falls short

T3.parameter: mu_L - mu_S = difference in host-level mean rating (each host's established entire homes averaged, every host counted once)
T3.why: same scale and threshold as T1; this test removes within-host dependence by design instead of by a model

T4.parameter: delta = within-stratum gap in mean accuracy score, hyped minus plain (strata: borough x host class; one listing per host)
T4.test: stratified permutation test (labels permuted within strata, 10,000 permutations); 95% CI by stratified bootstrap
T4.why: two-sided because exploration showed no direction (accuracy 4.775 with no hype word vs 4.777-4.799 with some); Airbnb shows category scores such as accuracy to one decimal, so a smaller gap is invisible to a guest
